analogs.covers: Social life: the sett, a dominant sow and boar, bold sentries, pushy at food
Temper and habits: flees danger without young, turns ferocious around them, mud wallows, rooting diet

headline: A badger sett in a ceratopsian body: sow-led, bold sentries, pushy at food, and as fierce as a wild-boar sow once cubs are around.

setting.label: Mixed ceratopsian herds, riverside mud in the dry season
setting.note: Nomadic. The dry season pulls the sett to rivers, overturned roots and mud pits; the rainy season sends it inland to lush courtship areas. Claims small territories only around nests on the courtship grounds.

playsLike: You live in a sett: an unlimited group run by a dominant sow who chooses the dominant boar, held together by alliances and power politics. Without young you are a medium herbivore that flees Apex carnivores. Once cubs or ceratopsian adoptees are around, the whole sett turns aggressive, forms a defensive circle and up to four defenders chase predators down. In mixed herds with Pachyrhinosaurus, Styracosaurus and Psittacosaurus you are the watchful eye.

why.text: The group is literally called a sett, with sows, boars and cubs, and the dominant sow rules through her allies. This is the European badger's social world and its official inspiration.
Very good eyesight, first to broadcast a warning in mixed herds, and the dominant pair take night-watch shifts. A bold, alert little boss.
In the dry season the sett circles a food bush and drives rival herbivores off, as possessive as badgers at a food patch or a boar sounder at a feeder.
Flees Apex carnivores when no young are present, but stands, charges and chases when cubs are defended. It follows the wild-boar sow pattern: wary alone, dangerous with piglets.
Wallows in mud and shallow water to cool off and eats flowers, nuts, roots and fruit: a rooting, wallowing lifestyle.

notLike: Badgers dig burrows and are nocturnal; Albertaceratops is cathemeral and lives above ground in a big herd.
The defensive circle is a musk-ox tactic that it shares with Pachyrhinosaurus and Styracosaurus.
Badgers also eat earthworms and small animals; Albertaceratops is a strict herbivore (flowers, nuts, roots, fruit).
